source_A_observation: A co-immunoprecipitation band was interpreted as MDM2 binding to p53 retrogene 9 after DNA damage.
source_B: Sulak et al. 2016 eLife and author response
source_B_observation: Authors argued the JAMA band was not at the expected MDM2 size, found no MDM2 co-IP with TP53RTG12, and linked loss of binding to family-wide W23G.
identity_relation: Sulak author response reports 100% nucleotide and protein identity between Abegglen RTG9 and TP53RTG12.
unresolved_question: Does the same 180-aa sequence bind MDM2, and is the answer dependent on assay or cell context?
required_resolution: Matched WT/G23W constructs, orthogonal MDM2 assays and standardized expression context.

source_A_observation: W23G and TP53 interaction support an MDM2-escape/guardian model.
source_B: Preston et al. 2023 Cell Death Discovery
source_B_observation: p53-R9 induces Tid1/Bax-associated mitochondrial apoptosis without requiring canonical transcriptional activity.
identity_relation: Both literatures concern the 180-aa elephant TP53 retrogene candidate but do not causally connect W23G to the mitochondrial phenotype.
unresolved_question: Is MDM2 escape causal for apoptosis, merely additive, or mechanistically separate?
required_resolution: G23W reversion measured across MDM2, turnover and mitochondrial endpoints in the same experiment.

source_A_observation: Mechanistic observations rely substantially on heterologous construct expression.
source_B_observation: Reviewers warned that overexpression and HEK293 p53 context can distort mechanistic interpretation.
identity_relation: Construct-intrinsic and endogenous-context questions are different experimental layers.
unresolved_question: Does the construct effect persist in elephant cells with canonical TP53 and endogenous regulation?
required_resolution: Two-phase design: p53-null construct-intrinsic phase followed by elephant-cell guardian validation.
